answer: New identities start under a probationary earning cap: they collect only a small share of each epoch's emission until they build a public history of graded contributions. Lifting the cap early requires locking an escalating stake that rises with each additional identity an operator runs, like a reef growing denser further out. An attacker faces a crystal-clear trade: wait out a long horizon of capped earnings per fake, or post so much stake per identity that the attack costs more than the capped rewards repay. Honest agents pay the wait once and keep full rate forever.
